{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/penguins.csv')

# Check the unique values of species and island
print('Unique species:', df['species'].unique())
print('Unique islands:', df['island'].unique())

# Cross-tabulate species and island to see the association
ct = pd.crosstab(df['species'], df['island'])
print('\nCross-tabulation of species by island:\n', ct)

# Compute mean flipper length by species within each island
df_grouped = df.groupby(['island', 'species'])['flipper_length_mm'].mean().reset_index()
print('\nMean flipper length by island and species:\n', df_grouped)

# Now, for each island, identify the species with the highest mean flipper length
max_flipper_by_island = df_grouped.loc[df_grouped.groupby('island')['flipper_length_mm'].idxmax()]
print('\nSpecies with highest mean flipper length in each island:\n', max_flipper_by_island)

# Finally, determine which species has the highest mean flipper length overall, but now we know the pattern per island
# We can now see whether one species consistently leads across islands
max_flipper_by_species = df_grouped.groupby('species')['flipper_length_mm'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
print('\nOverall mean flipper length by species (stratified by island):\n', max_flipper_by_species)"}
